title: Why use a custom pool with CompletableFuture
context: Why should you pass your own executor to CompletableFuture methods?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Without an executor argument, supplyAsync and the *Async methods use ForkJoinPool.commonPool(). That pool is shared by the whole JVM and sized to the CPU count, so slow I/O tasks can starve parallel streams and other libraries. Pass a dedicated ThreadPoolExecutor for blocking work, with a named ThreadFactory and bounded queue, so the impact stays contained and you can monitor it.

points.title: Shared common pool
points.why: The default pool is shared across the JVM and sized for CPU work, not blocking I/O.

points.title: Isolation
points.why: A dedicated executor keeps slow calls from starving other code.
